chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman from whom he mentioned from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who gave another man money to perform Hajj for him, and an event occurred to that man, he said: 'If he had set out and it happened to him during part of the journey, it is sufficient for the first one; otherwise, no.'

Because the meaning in this report is also that the event occurs to him after entering the Haram, and the report does not explicitly state whether it was before or after entering, and it is possible for what we mentioned.
Al-Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And when a person performs Hajj on behalf of another, let him say after finishing from the ghusl of Ihram.

key_terms.اَلْحَدَثُ: an event/incident (such as death or illness)
key_terms.يَحِجُّهُ: to perform Hajj on behalf of him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if the proxy performing Hajj on behalf of someone else dies during the journey?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the validity of Hajj performed by a proxy (na'ib) when interrupted by death or impediment, establishing that the obligation is discharged for the principal regardless of whether the event occurs before or after entering the Haram. Sheikh al-Tusi’s commentary highlights the juristic nuance of timing, while also prescribing the specific supplication after the ghusl of Ihram, reflecting the Shia emphasis on ritual precision in proxy worship. This ruling underscores the concept of *ada'* (fulfillment) in Hajj, where the physical completion by the agent suffices for the one who commissioned it.
